## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Roblox-style animation and character-customization game with 100 worlds, model creation for video scenes, customizable eyes and mouth, extensive clothing and hair, and a skin color wheel.

## Requirements
- Implement the game directly without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- User’s concept includes “1000000 clothes and hair” and a color wheel for skin color.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based 3D block-character studio using Three.js, with procedurally generated worlds and character assets.

## Work State

### Completed
- Created `index.html` with responsive studio UI: avatar customization, face selectors, wardrobe, animation controls, timeline, worlds panel, model-builder panel, and dialogs.
- Created `game.js` with 3D character and world rendering, 100 world names, character color and outfit customization, animation modes, model creation and drag positioning, project saving/loading, and timeline controls.
- Verified `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser smoke-tested: page title is `BLOCKSTAR — Animation Studio`; worlds panel contains 100 cards; model builder successfully adds a model.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/game.jpg`.

### Active
- Continue implementation and verify the latest edits. The last change added an outfit color input in `index.html`, but its JavaScript handler has not been added yet.
- Test responsive layout and browser interactions; ensure no JavaScript errors beyond the favicon 404.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add an `#outfitTint` handler in `game.js` that applies color to the selected clothing category/material and updates the wardrobe preview.
2. Run `node --check game.js`, reload in Playwright, test wardrobe tinting, face controls, world selection, save/restore, and mobile layout.
3. Refresh and inspect `screenshots/game.jpg`; report the implemented features and any reasonable scope assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main studio interface and styles.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, gameplay/customization logic, and project persistence.
- `screenshots/game.jpg`: Latest inspected browser screenshot.

## Important Context
- Local dev server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; browser URL is `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright browser was installed after initial failure: `Browser "chromium" is not installed`.
- Changes are uncommitted.
